messages:
maria: heads-up — during onboarding FP8 candidate (redwood/falcon-7b-fp8-v2) I see weird ANSI escape tokens in outputs for our email->JSON parser tests. Example below.

maria: ```
Subject: \x1b[31mUrgent:\x1b[0m Please confirm
Body: Hello,
Please find attached.
---
Parsed JSON:
{"subject": "\x1b[31mUrgent:\x1b[0m Please confirm", "body": "Hello, Please find attached."}
```

devan: when did this start? AWQ/GPTQ/FP8 only?

maria: only FP8 runs so far (+ a plain int8 run). fp16 baseline is clean. Repro steps: eval-harness --suite=email-json --seed=42 --model=redwood/falcon-7b-fp8-v2. Observed: F1 down ~6.2%, formatting errors +18% (subject field tokenization).

lee: logs: https://internal.ci/jobs/2981#run-12 :eyes:

quant-bot: [automated] FP8 calibration job 2981 completed (exit 0). profile: layerwise scale suggested.

sophie: sounds like serialization noise — could be KV-cache alignment or rounding leaking into tokenization. Also check tokenizer pre/post-processing for ANSI escapes :thinking_face:

infra-bot: FYI we rolled a new kernel optimization on 3032103000 that touches fast-math and fused-attn kernels.

maria: I can repro locally when I enable --fast-kernel. If I run with --no-fast-math the escapes stop appearing but performance degrades.

devan: can you run a short calibration sweep? try layer-wise bias correction: quant-sweep --layers 1-12 --bias-scale 0.0,0.05,0.1

maria: running now, will paste numbers shortly.

maria: quick results: bias-scale=0.1 recovers ~4.8% F1 (not fully), formatting errors drop to +6%. ANSI escapes still appear on subjects containing markup-like tokens. hypothesis: fused kernel rounding causes off-by-one token ids for tokens like "\x1b" sequence which then surface as literal escapes in model output.

devan: interesting. next steps: (1) reproduce with deterministic seed across kernels (2) try GPTQ candidate (3) add eval case with control chars to our regression suite. I'll open a ticket.

devan: @sophie can you add control-char tests to email-json suite?

sophie: on it, will add a small test set and a canary that runs on every quant candidate.

maria: thanks — filing notes in the ticket and attaching the failing prompts. :thumbsup:
